statistic: As v1 (session-clustered mean net USD per session, Student-t CI with sessions-1 df, full P&L decomposition), plus ticks_behind_touch_{mean,median,max} and frac_decisions_skew_changed_quote per cell.
validity_gate: Before any P&L is read: a skewed cell is VALID only if frac_decisions_skew_changed_quote >= 0.10 (pooled over its test units); an invalid cell reports 'skew inert' and gets no verdict.
verdict_rule: As v1: quoting edge EXISTS for a cell iff mean net USD/session > 0 AND its Bonferroni CI over the 4 cells excludes 0 AND >= 4 of 6 test sessions have quote fills. Skew HELPS iff mean(skewed - control) > 0 with its Bonferroni CI excluding 0 (testable only on VALID cells). In-sample: EXISTS reads 'worth an out-of-sample test'. No tuning after results; no sweep.

alpha_weight_derivation: skew_ticks = round(alpha_weight * er * mid / tick). On the 7 in-sample sessions (continuous trading, LinearAlpha fitted on all 7, score() with the pinned clip) the per-symbol median |er|*mid/tick was: EQ01 AAPL 0.136 / MSFT 0.077 / QQQ 0.087; EQ05 0.063 / 0.035 / 0.037; EQ10 AAPL 0.066 / MSFT 0.043. alpha_weight = 0.5 / min(median) rounded up, so every symbol's median |skew| is >= 1 tick: EQ01 7 (need 6.5), EQ05 15 (14.2), EQ10 12 (11.5). This deliberately scales the forecasts 7-15x so the skew can move quotes; it is a design constant, not a fitted edge.
